source.title: FIRM: Fisher-Informed Retention Merging for Federated LLM Unlearning
source.authors: Reeyansh Shah; Maram Hasan; Subhasis Chaudhuri; Biplab Banerjee

record.file_problem: The full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study extends LLM unlearning evaluation to federated aggregation and reports targeted-task performance and retained utility. It does not test recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates unlearning outcomes, not post-unlearning recovery. It does not apply fine-tuning recovery sets, activation-direction ablation, post-unlearning quantization, or prompt-based recovery. Its use of a 4-bit NF4 model for primary experiments is not a quantization attack. Related-work descriptions of other unlearning methods are not results from this study.
record.test_reason: This is a federated unlearning method paper (FIRM). It uses the original sources' tools, the WMDP benchmark and an RMU-style objective, and reports only how well its own merge and the baselines forget and keep utility. It applies no recovery attack: no relearning fine-tuning, no direction ablation, no quantization of the unlearned model, no prompting attack. So it cannot bear on whether unlearning is shallow or robust. The 4-bit NF4 loading is a training-efficiency choice, not a quantization attack. The forgetting and utility numbers are the method's own performance, not a test of version A as stated. I disagree with the reader's 'tests/T3'.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that FIRM's Fisher-normalized merge improves utility at comparable measured forgetting on WMDP and MUSE-HP, with metric-dependent trade-offs on TOFU. Retention projection adds gains only at selected operating points. They also caution that zero ROUGE-L 'concerns the evaluated answers, not proof of complete knowledge removal'. They do not test whether the knowledge can be recovered.
record.recipe_differences: FIRM is a federated adapter-merging and retention-control method, not one of the original centralized unlearning recipes. It uses local RMU-style training on WMDP and gradient ascent on TOFU and MUSE-HP, then performs Fisher-informed server-side aggregation.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported forgetting–utility outcomes vary with global scale gamma, benchmark, and model. Retention-projection tolerance also changes the trade-off in separate experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: On WMDP/Zephyr, merges that reach near-chance accuracy collapse MMLU utility: FULM at gamma 0.3 (Bio 24.59, Util 23.46), AVG (24.18), TIES (22.80). FIRM-base reaches at best Bio 32.60 with Util 40.43 (pretrained 54.46).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In federated adapter merging, near-chance WMDP forgetting comes with large utility loss. This is a trade-off in forgetting efficacy, not a recovery result.

record.problems: No recovery attack is evaluated, so the study cannot establish whether knowledge is hidden or removed. WMDP remains above the stated chance accuracy for the reported FIRM-base sweep. TOFU and MUSE-HP use ROUGE-L rather than chance-referenced accuracy; the authors explicitly caution that zero MUSE-HP ROUGE-L is not proof of complete knowledge removal. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the main sweeps.
record.rows_left_out: Within the 60-row limit, omitted FIRM-base WMDP gamma=0.50 rows (Table 1), MUSE-HP gamma=0.30 and 0.50 rows (Table 4), TOFU Real Authors and Real World metrics (Table 3), FULM and other aggregation-baseline result rows (Tables 1–4), and supplementary cross-model, ablation, scale-matched, and retention-projection results (Tables 5–16 and Appendix A.1). These results do not report recovery attacks. The selected rows prioritize references and primary FIRM-base benchmark outcomes.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks recover the knowledge is never tested. Forgetting and utility are reported only as the method's own performance.
No activation-direction ablation or block-vs-delete analysis.
No quantization of the unlearned model. NF4 is used only for training.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context recovery.
FIRM does not claim or test robustness to recovery attacks.

record.verdict_notes: All reader rows used the invalid version id 'V1'; every row is relinked to none. The reader's two limits_scope labels for A are dropped: they rest on the method's own performance with no recovery test. The 4-bit NF4 loading is not a quantization attack on the unlearned model.

versions.untested_parts: Tests targeted-task performance and retained utility for federated unlearning, but does not test whether simple attacks recover knowledge. MUSE-HP reports ROUGE-L rather than accuracy, so it cannot establish near-chance accuracy.
No recovery fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact examples.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis showing that unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual, or in-context recovery evaluation.
FIRM addresses federated merging and retention; the paper does not claim or test resistance to the recovery attacks listed in the claim.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: WMDP on Zephyr-7Bβ across the reported FIRM-base scales
reader_labels.reason: The reported WMDP accuracies remain above the stated 25% chance level; at the strongest forgetting setting utility falls to 40.43% from the 54.46% pretrained reference (W06-Bio through W12-Util). The paper does not evaluate recovery attacks.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: TOFU on Zephyr-7Bβ at the reported FIRM-base scales
reader_labels.reason: Retain-set scores stay near the expert reference, but forget-set ROUGE-L remains 70.00–90.15% at the recorded settings and is not a chance-level accuracy test (T1-Fgt through T16-Util).
